label: input token b at original-phase position >= 3 (magnitude grows with position)
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is b during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 3; every such step fires (precision 1.0). Silent for b at t = 0..2, on the delimiter, during the copy phase (including when b is fed back or output), and on all other tokens (a handful of stray firings on n/t/etc.). Magnitude rises roughly linearly with position: about 0.23 of max at t=3, ~0.45-0.5 at t=4, ~0.65 at t=5, ~0.8 at t=6, ~0.94 at t=7, ~1.0 at t=8, regardless of L or the preceding tokens. A repeated b is slightly less likely to be the first occurrence, but repeats still fire.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split the predicate has 0 false positives. Its 64 missed activations hold 0.0% of the activation mass. They are tiny firings (0.01-0.02 of max) at step 8 on tokens z, t, 2, g, n, i, i.e. scattered noise.
Profile confirms the factual claims: 0 firings in the delimiter and copy phases, 0 firings at t=0..2, and 57557 of 57601 active steps are on input b.
The magnitude-growth claim holds. Activation mass per firing rises from about 0.119/16208 at t=3 to about 0.081/2848 at t=8, roughly a 4x increase, which matches 0.23 -> 1.0 of max.

No dependence on prev_tok, first_tok or in_count, so the claim that repeated b's still fire and that it holds across contexts checks out. L=3 has no firings only because t>=3 does not exist in the original phase for L=3.
